kanban-claude 0.4.0.dev4

A worker may now make the PR writes its own protocol asks for, and kanban request-review adds a missing Closes line itself instead of throwing finished work away. A foreground gate call may run for 30 minutes, not 10. kanban stats stops hiding the returns the owner made. A gate sha no longer stands for a repo without green CI.

Release explainer, 2026-11-01. Diff v0.4.0.dev3 (490a99b) to 3a09050, the merge of PR #21. This is a pre-release. The version bump to 0.4.0.dev4, the changelog section and the releases row come after the diff and are not part of it.

  • 26 of 29

    blocked/capability runs on the jobbot board were finished work — green gate, open PR — thrown away over one missing line

  • 202 of 434

    gate runs hit the old 10-minute foreground Bash cap and then spent turns polling their own backgrounded run

  • 10 of 46

    card returns in a 7-day window were invisible in kanban stats, because the guards block counted only the reviewer's verdicts

  • 2

    merged PRs, #20 and #21, with 6 commits; +175 and −40 lines in 19 files

  • +5

    test functions; no new config key, no schema change, 1129 tests green on CPython 3.14

Background

Where these changes came from

0.4.0.dev3 shipped the stall watchdog, wait-ci's honest exits and the Closes requirement. Running them on a live board (jobbot, 327 done cards) showed that two of those guards were costing more work than they saved, and that the board's own numbers were understating how often a card came back. The evidence is the board's task_runs and task_events tables, not an impression.

  • A guard that threw finished work away. 29 runs ended blocked/capability. 26 of them had a green gate and an open PR: request-review refused the card because its PR body lacked Closes OWNER/REPO#N, told the builder to run gh pr edit, and --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none then refused that edit as an external system write. One run's own words: “The auto-mode classifier denied gh pr edit 588 --body-file $TMPDIR/body.md (reason: External System Writes)”. Permission denials by role: smith 99, warden 9, scout 2.
  • A ceiling the gate could not fit under. 202 of 434 gate runs hit claude's 10-minute foreground Bash cap. The agent then backgrounded the suite and burned turns on pgrep and tail, which is slower and noisier than waiting.
  • A statistic that flattered the board. changes_requested events came from two actors: worker 39 and owner:cli 12. The guards block in kanban stats counted only the first, so a card the owner sent back himself still read as a first-pass approval.
  • A card-authoring mistake, not a dispatcher bug. 4 of 39 reviewer send-backs were a second Alembic head. dispatcher.touches_overlap already matches directory prefixes; the cards had each declared their own new migration filename, and two new filenames never overlap.

PR #20 is the separate gate-evidence fix: a pre-flight that cleared a stale Gate: line on a repo with no CI, so an old sha could speak for an untested head. PR #21 carries the rest. Line numbers are in the files at the head of this diff.

Change diagram

Which components changed, and how

  • + added
  • ~ changed
  • ! fixed
  • = left as it was

Boxes are components; each row is one change. Nothing new was added between components: the two protocol fixes move work from the agent, which cannot do it, to the CLI and the settings file, which can.

Walkthrough

Six changes, one at a time

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

The CLI writes the Closes line instead of refusing the card !fixed+added

What changed
_closes() (worker.py:110) no longer raises Refused with a gh pr edit command for the builder to run. It appends the line itself: it keeps whatever the builder wrote, separated by a blank line, and calls the new ghops.pr_set_body(), which runs gh pr edit <n> --repo <repo> --body-file - with the text on stdin. gh_rc() gained a stdin parameter for it, passed through as input=, so a body with backticks or $ never reaches a shell. A refusal is still raised, but only when the edit itself fails, and it names the gh error.
Why
The requirement was right and the enforcement was in the wrong process. The builder runs under --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none, where the classifier reads gh pr edit as an external system write and turns the question into a refusal; the guard therefore asked for the one thing the agent was forbidden to do. 26 of 29 blocked/capability runs died there with the work already finished. kanban request-review is a plain subprocess, outside the classifier, so the line costs it nothing.
How you notice it
A linked card whose PR body lacks the line now gets it appended during request-review, and the run continues to review. agents/smith.md and agents/designer.md say the CLI appends it, “so a missing line is no reason to block”. Tests: test_request_review_adds_the_closes_line_a_linked_cards_pr_lacks and test_request_review_refuses_when_the_closes_line_cannot_be_added in test_worker.py; the fake gh in conftest.py grew a pr edit branch that reads stdin and honours GH_FAKE_EDIT_FAIL.

A worker may make the PR writes its own protocol asks for +added

What changed
PROTOCOL_RULES (runner.py:69) is a new module constant, ("Bash(gh pr create:*)", "Bash(gh pr edit:*)", "Bash(gh pr comment:*)"), and the run's settings file now carries "permissions": {"deny": deny, "allow": [*PROTOCOL_RULES, *rules]} (:179). Those three commands are exactly what the run protocol tells a builder and a warden to do: open the PR, put the gate evidence in its body, post the review ledger. Bash(gh pr merge:*) stays in the deny list, and a deny outranks an allow, so a worker still cannot merge its own PR.
Why
Same mechanism as above, seen from the settings side: --permission-mode auto classifies any gh write as an external system write, and --permission-prompts none makes that a refusal rather than a question. A builder asked to write its own PR body had no way to comply. This is the belt to request-review's suspenders; the Closes fix above is what removes the 26 lost runs.
How you notice it
Nothing in the board changes. test_runner.py adds test_the_protocol_may_write_its_own_pr_but_still_cannot_merge_it, and the argv contract test now asserts the allow list is [*runner.PROTOCOL_RULES, "Bash(npm publish)"].

A gate may run for 30 minutes in the foreground ~changed+added

What changed
The runner sets BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS to store.BASH_CAP_MS (1 800 000). Setting the default alone does nothing: claude clamps it to its own 600 s maximum, which a probe confirms — with both set, a worker reads “timeout is in milliseconds: default 1800000, max 1800000”. store.py gained BASH_CAP_MS and STALL_MIN_S = BASH_CAP_MS // 1000 + 100 (1900 s) above DEFAULTS, so the watchdog floor is derived from the cap rather than written twice; worker.stall_s now defaults to STALL_MIN_S + 500 (2400 s) and its refusal message interpolates the cap. measure.py records BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS with the other run parameters.
Why
202 of 434 gate runs took longer than 10 minutes. The cap did not make them faster; it pushed the agent into backgrounding the suite and polling it, which costs turns and hides failures. The stall floor has to move with the cap, because a foreground call is silent by design for as long as the cap allows, and a watchdog below the cap would kill a healthy run.
How you notice it
skills/kanban/SKILL.md now says the stall default is 40 minutes. A board that set worker.stall_s by hand keeps its own value — see the upgrade notes. test_store.py's stall tests read store.STALL_MIN_S instead of a literal, and test_the_stall_floor_outlives_the_longest_quiet_call ties the two constants together so neither can move alone.

kanban stats counts the returns the owner made +added

What changed
_measure_stats (store.py) builds a second window clause from the first — where.replace("r.started_at", "e.created_at").replace("t.board", "e.board") — and counts owner_reopens and cards_owner_reopened from task_events where kind='changes_requested' AND actor NOT LIKE 'worker:%'. Both appear in the guards block beside send_backs. first_pass_rate is left alone: it is the reviewer's metric and should stay comparable.
Why
A card the owner sent back is a return like any other, and the block that exists to say how often work comes back was silent about it. Measured on the live board over 7 days: 36 reviewer send-backs reported, 46 real returns. The web dashboard needed no change — webui/stats.js:233 renders the guards block generically through kv(), so the two new keys appear by themselves.
How you notice it
kanban stats --board <b> prints the two new keys. test_measure.py's guards test now writes an owner reopen and asserts it is counted separately.

A gate sha stops standing for a repo without green CI !fixed~changed

What changed
PR #20. The review pre-flight (skills/kanban-code-review/scripts/preflight.py) used to clear a stale Gate: sha whenever the sha was an ancestor of the head with only merge commits since. That reasoning only holds if CI tested the merged tree, so the ok now requires every check on the head to have passed; with no green CI the line is a CHECK and the warden runs the gate on the head itself. smith and designer now write the “no CI covers the merged head” note on the line below Gate:, and never name the head on the Gate: line, because pre-flight reads every sha on that line and one matching the head reads as a gate run that happened.

And a test fix. The autouse fixture fakes macOS by setting sys.platform, and on CPython 3.14 urllib.request runs its one-time _scproxy import under that fake the first time something imports it lazily (Path.as_uri() in web.py), which fails on Linux: every test in test_web.py returned 500. conftest.py now imports urllib.request before any fake is in place.
Why
The gate evidence is the one thing a reviewer cannot re-derive cheaply, so a sha that proves nothing is worse than no sha. The builder-side wording change exists because the old note was ambiguous: a head sha anywhere on the Gate: line was read as a gate run.
How you notice it
On a repo with no workflows, pre-flight prints a CHECK for the gate line and the warden runs the gate. test_preflight.py covers the green and not-green heads.

card-checker names the directory, not the file it would add ~changed

What changed
agents/card-checker.md:46: on a card's touches: line, a file the card adds is named by its directory (alembic/versions/), not by the new filename.
Why
4 of 39 reviewer send-backs were a second Alembic head. dispatcher.touches_overlap already matches directory prefixes, so the dispatcher would have held the second card — but each card had declared its own new migration filename, and two filenames that do not exist yet never overlap. The fix belongs in how cards are written, not in the guard.
How you notice it
Two cards that both add a migration now show skipped: touches_overlap instead of racing. There is no Python test for agent text.

Known limits

What this release does not do

  • The PROTOCOL_RULES allow is not proven against the classifier. The 30-minute cap was confirmed with a probe; no run yet shows that an allow rule in --settings beats --permission-mode auto's external-write refusal. What demonstrably removes the lost runs is request-review writing the line itself.
  • A stored worker.stall_s is not raised. config_set validates on write only, and the runner reads the stored value without checking it, so a board that set 1200 by hand under 0.4.0.dev3 keeps a watchdog below the new Bash cap. Raise it yourself — see the upgrade notes.
  • Base divergence is still the reviewer's problem. About 36% of reviewer send-backs are textual conflicts with the base or a duplicate migration head, and most arise while the PR sits in review, after the builder finished. smith merges origin/<base> before review (step 12), which does not help a PR that goes stale afterwards. No provision-time merge was added: it would help only a re-run, and it would be the daemon's first write to a card branch.
  • No base-aware overlap guard. It was measured and dropped: 0 of 856 skip events have two different explicit bases, and only 12 events over 8 cards (1.4%) are genuinely wrong holds.
  • no_ci is still asked per run. Caching it per repo would re-open the hole PR #20 just closed, because the 60 s grace is the only protection against an external GitHub App registering a status late. The real fix is CI on the board's repos.

Upgrade notes

Moving from 0.4.0.dev3 to 0.4.0.dev4

  1. Run /kanban-claude:setup between cards so the daemon and the CLI move together. The schema stays at 7: no migration, no backup. A run that began under 0.4.0.dev3 keeps the old 10-minute Bash cap and the old stall limit.
  2. Check your stall setting: kanban config get worker.stall_s. If it prints a stored value below 1900, the watchdog will stop a healthy 30-minute gate call as stalled. Fix it with kanban config set worker.stall_s 2400. A board that never set the key gets the new default and needs nothing.
  3. The plugin's cache is keyed by version, so /plugin update on an unchanged version is a no-op and the agent prompts stay old. Updating to a new version is what deploys the smith, designer and card-checker text in this release.
  4. kanban stats gains owner_reopens and cards_owner_reopened in the guards block. Earlier windows are recomputed from task_events, so historical numbers change the first time you look.

Range covered

The diff runs from the tag v0.4.0.dev3 (490a99b) to 3a09050: 6 commits and 2 merged PRs, 19 files, +175 and −40 lines.

  • d67f22d, 7736485, a8f0756, 53b05b6 the urllib.request import, the stale gate sha, the changelog, the no-CI note below the Gate line (PR #20)
  • 416cd03 stop throwing finished runs away over a PR body line, and let a gate run to the end (PR #21)
  • 78aaa73 let a worker make the PR writes its own protocol asks for (PR #21)

Neither PR had a merge conflict. The version bump, the changelog section and the releases row come after the range.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Five questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. A linked card's PR body has no Closes line when the builder calls kanban request-review. What happens?

The first answer is what 0.4.0.dev3 did, and it cost 26 of 29 blocked/capability runs their finished work: the builder could not run gh pr edit, because --permission-mode auto reads it as an external system write. The CLI is a plain subprocess, outside that classifier.

2. Why does the runner set BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS as well as BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS?

Measured with a probe: with both set, the worker's tool description reads “default 1800000, max 1800000”. With only the default set, the cap stays at 600 s and 202 of 434 gate runs hit it.

3. Your board has worker.stall_s set to 1200 from dev3. You upgrade. What should you do?

config_set validates on write only and the runner reads the stored value as it finds it, so the new floor applies to new writes, not to old ones. This is listed as a known limit.

4. Two cards each add a new Alembic migration. Under this release, what keeps them from colliding?

dispatcher.touches_overlap already matched directory prefixes. The bug was in how the cards were written: two filenames that do not exist yet never overlap. The base-aware guard was measured and dropped — 1.4% of holds are genuinely wrong.

5. A PR's Gate: line names a sha that is an ancestor of the head, with only merge commits since, and the repo has no workflows. What does the review pre-flight say?

The ancestor reasoning only holds if some run tested the merged tree, and on a repo with no CI nothing did. This is PR #20.
